# What hosted CI actually checks, and what it does not.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. .github/workflows/build.yml produces five green checks
# on every commit to main. A reader who sees five green checks reasonably
# concludes the commit was fully verified. It was not: the test suite never runs
# hosted. Nothing anywhere said so in a form a machine could check, so the gap
# was invisible to exactly the person the checks exist to inform — someone who
# does not trust this machine and is reading the commit on GitHub.
#
# This file is the declared coverage, and tools/lint/check_verification_coverage.sh
# holds it to the workflow. It cannot drift: every item claiming to be hosted
# must name a job key that really exists in build.yml, and every job in build.yml
# must be claimed by some item. Adding a job without declaring what it verifies
# fails lint; claiming an item is hosted when its job was renamed or deleted
# fails lint.
#
# THE FIVE ITEMS ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE HERE. The gate hard-codes the required item
# list (gcc, clang, lint, tests, fuzz-replay) in its own file, so the gap cannot
# be closed by deleting a row. That two files must agree is the point — the same
# discipline check_promotion_receipt_chain.sh prong 6 documents, added there
# after a mutation reworded a message and a same-file self-test still passed.
#
# Format — five `|`-separated fields, one item per line:
#
#   item | hosted | job_key | display_name | attested_by
#
#   item          short name of the verification item.
#   hosted        exactly `yes` or `no`. Nothing else parses.
#   job_key       the YAML key under `jobs:` in build.yml when hosted=yes;
#                 exactly `-` when hosted=no. NOT the display name: matrix job
#                 names are templated (`compile-check (${{ matrix.cc }})`) and
#                 never appear literally in the file, so a display-name match
#                 would be checking a string that is not there.
#   display_name  the check name a reader sees on GitHub, for humans only.
#   attested_by   where the verdict comes from when hosted=no. Must be
#                 non-empty; `-` when hosted=yes. An item that is not hosted and
#                 does not say who vouches for it is an unverified claim.
#
# CONFIRMATION STATUS — read this before quoting any row as verified.
#
# The gcc, clang, lint, fuzz-replay and compile-all-tus rows were each confirmed
# against a real check-run attached to commit df752afce on origin/main (run
# 30509201499, all five success).
#
# The `tests` row is hosted and RED. `hosted=yes` here means only what the gate
# can check — that a job with that key exists in build.yml and this file claims
# it. It does NOT mean the job goes green, and right now it does not. Anyone
# reading a commit on GitHub should treat the suite as hosted-but-failing until
# this paragraph says otherwise.
#
# First hosted run: 30516674384, commit be432065d, 2026-07-30. The other five
# jobs succeeded. `tests` FAILED in 10m52s — not a timeout; the job limit is 120
# minutes, so a hosted runner carries this suite comfortably. Its own verdict
# line: groups_total=846 groups_ran=842 groups_gated=4 groups_failed=6
# self_skips=25, 308.2s wall, 4 workers.
#
# Six groups failed, in three classes. This is what the job was built to find.
#
#  1. READS THE DEFAULT DATADIR — a real defect, not a runner quirk.
#     test_chain_integrity_failed_condition never calls SetDataDir, so it
#     resolves to ~/.zclassic-c23 and the runner logged
#     `cannot open /home/runner/.zclassic-c23/blocks/blk00000.dat`. On the
#     maintainer host that path is the LIVE NODE and is populated, so the test
#     has been passing by reading the live node's block files: silently
#     weakened, and touching a datadir no test may touch. An independent
#     machine proved it; the maintainer host structurally cannot.
#
#  2. REQUIRES THE SAPLING PARAMETERS — test_proof_validate_stage (joinsplit_sig
#     case) and test_pv_lookahead. `read_file failed for sapling-spend.params`.
#     These need a ~770 MB artifact that is not in the repository and is not
#     fetched by CI, and unlike the params_missing case in the same file — which
#     passes, because it is written for absent params — they do not self-skip.
#
#  3. UNDIAGNOSED, possibly real ordering bugs. test_block_status_event_restart_proof
#     (2 assertions: `boundary height never falsely reported complete`,
#     `fixture fully folded`), test_zcode_policy (`corrupt wires skipped and
#     counted, facts intact`), and test_make_lint_gates_shard_08 (`P1-3 systemd
#     memory budget: baseline and selftest pass`, baseline_rc != 0). No error is
#     printed for the first two; they may be assumptions about scheduling or
#     readdir order that only hold on the maintainer host. Nothing here has been
#     root-caused yet and none of it is claimed to be environmental.
#
# The permitted resolutions are unchanged: fix the coupling (classes 1 and 3),
# or declare a smaller hosted scope IN THIS FILE naming exactly what is excluded
# and why (class 2, where the blocker is an artifact nobody ships). Class 2 may
# self-skip only if the skip is loud and counted — a skip that coasts silently
# has already cost this project a week of hollow green. The dishonest
# resolutions, ruled out: trimming the corpus until it passes, gating on a
# narrow tail/grep instead of the full output, or editing this paragraph to
# assert a confirmation that did not happen.

gcc|yes|compile-check|compile-check (gcc)|-
clang|yes|compile-check|compile-check (clang)|-
lint|yes|lint|lint (make lint)|-
fuzz-replay|yes|fuzz-replay|fuzz-replay (saved findings)|-
compile-all-tus|yes|build|build (cached dependencies)|-
tests|yes|tests|tests (make test-parallel)|-
